column4: Arabic is written from right to left in letters that join one another; only the long vowels are written, the short ones can be added as small marks above and below (harakat).

column2: The Arabic alphabet of 28 letters, grown from the Nabataean form of the Aramaic script; the oldest dated Arabic inscriptions are of the 4th–6th centuries, and the Qurʾan fixed its classical form.

Type as it sounds: th, kh, dh, sh, gh for ث خ ذ ش غ, ' for the hamza ء and ` for ʿayn ع. Long vowels twice (aa, ii, uu) or with a line (ā ī ū) become ا ي و; short vowels are not written unless “Vowel marks” is on. A hyphen joins words, as in al-kitāb.
